meta.title: Sentinel Threat Timeline 2026
meta.description: Publicly reported critical vulnerabilities, exploits, breaches, supply-chain incidents, PKI failures, and AI-related security events from 1 January 2026 through 25 October 2026. Includes PHP2Shell, Railway, Hugging Face agent intrusion, eMudhra weak CA keys, and more.
meta.disclaimer: Public reporting only. Not a complete CVE database. Dates prefer official announcement or widely confirmed disclosure. Severities follow vendor/CISA ratings where available. No exploit instructions included.
meta.note: Curated HIGH-IMPACT public events only (critical runtimes, frameworks, PKI, major supply-chain, large breaches, AI-agent incidents). Not a complete catalog of mid-size or small ransomware claims, local notices, or every leak-site listing. Public trackers list hundreds of 2026 incidents; this timeline prioritizes events most relevant to web operators and Sentinel users.

events.title: Pizza Hut Japan customer data breach
events.subtitle: Customer information exposed
events.summary: Pizza Hut Japan disclosed a data breach exposing customer information.

events.title: GoDaddy revokes 404,607 SSL certificates after policy errors
events.subtitle: Mass revocation including some government sites
events.summary: GoDaddy revoked 404,607 SSL/TLS certificates after finding certificate-policy errors. Affected sites included some Gibraltar government websites.

events.title: Capcom CAPCOM ID breach — 11.7 million accounts
events.subtitle: Email addresses and login metadata exposed
events.summary: Unauthorized access to CAPCOM ID membership service. About 11.77 million records with email addresses and associated metadata; passwords changed on a small number of accounts without authorization.
events.impact: Players of Capcom online services (Street Fighter, Monster Hunter, etc.).

exploitation.notes: Contained per company notices.

events.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup identities abused toward Microsoft 365 tenants
events.subtitle: China-linked activity using application identities; agentic AI mentioned in coverage
events.summary: Attackers abused application identities and secrets behind ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) to authenticate into customer Microsoft 365 tenants. Coverage linked China-linked actors and agentic AI assistance in related reporting.
events.impact: MSP customers using ConnectWise backup integrations with M365.

exploitation.notes: Third-party integration trust boundary failure.

events.title: PHP2Shell — two critical unauthenticated RCEs in PHP core
events.subtitle: CVE-2026-109618 & CVE-2026-109619
events.summary: Two critical unauthenticated RCEs in PHP core (PHP2Shell). CVE-2026-109618: RCE via out-of-memory corruption during request cleanup. CVE-2026-109619: RCE via stale global state reused across requests on the same worker. CVSS v4.0 9.2 each (NVD CVSS 3.1 often listed 9.8). Affects any SAPI serving web requests (mod_php, PHP-FPM, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed). WordPress/Drupal/Joomla/Magento all at risk because the bug is in PHP itself — app updates alone do not fix it. Fixed only in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35. EOL 8.1 and older: no official release (minimal source backports for 7.4/8.0/8.1). Exploitation attempts reported same week.
events.impact: Any internet-facing PHP site on unpatched runtime — remote code execution without login.

exploitation.notes: Exploit attempts observed by Cloudflare and others shortly after leak; public PoC material circulated.

events.sentinel_relevance: Primary reason Sentinel exists. Check sites for PHP exposure, version signals, and patch urgency.

events.title: Node.js October 2026 security release — Brotli RCE and TLS hostname bypasses
events.subtitle: 10 CVEs; lead issue CVE-2026-111497
events.summary: Node.js October 2026 security release: 10 CVEs across supported lines. Headline: CVE-2026-111497 — out-of-bounds write in the bundled Brotli decoder (malformed compressed input → crash / memory issues / possible RCE). Also high-severity TLS hostname validation bypasses (CVE-2026-106069, CVE-2026-105483). Fixed in Node.js 26.12.1, 24.22.1, 22.23.4. EOL lines (e.g. 20.x) received no fix in this release.
events.impact: Node services accepting attacker-controlled compressed data or relying on TLS hostname checks.

exploitation.notes: Public technical detail available; mass exploitation not confirmed as of late October 2026.

events.sentinel_relevance: Useful companion signal when a site shows Node/Next.js fingerprints.

events.title: GitLab CE/EE — dual critical RCEs (CVSS 10.0)
events.subtitle: CVE-2026-97229 (12 Oct) + CVE-2026-110264 (21 Oct, back to GitLab 7.0)
events.summary: Two separate maximum-severity GitLab waves in October 2026. 12 Oct: CVE-2026-97229 — integer overflow in CI/CD regex compiler enabling unauthenticated RCE (initial fixed builds 19.4.2 / 19.3.5 / 19.2.8 — still insufficient for the later bug). 21 Oct: CVE-2026-110264 — another CVSS 10.0 unauthenticated RCE affecting self-managed CE/EE from GitLab 7.0 (2014) through current; fixed in 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10, 18.11.13. Same releases also addressed XSS, auth flaws, and CI variable exposure issues. GitLab.com already patched; self-managed must upgrade again if only on the 12 Oct builds.
events.impact: Self-managed GitLab CE/EE — unauthenticated remote code execution.

exploitation.notes: Disclosed in the same critical week as PHP2Shell and Node.js releases.

events.sentinel_relevance: DevOps platform risk; not directly scanned by Sentinel but relevant to engineering teams.

events.title: Next.js critical remote code execution flaws
events.subtitle: Image Optimization API and use-cache typed-array issues
events.summary: Vercel out-of-band Next.js release fixing two unauthenticated RCE paths (CVSS ~9.5 class) plus Server Actions DoS. 1) RCE via use cache / React Server Components (GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr) on App Router with Cache Components (Next 16.0.0–16.4.0). 2) RCE via SVG/librsvg through sharp (CVE-2026-96889) when attacker SVGs reach image processing. Fixed in Next.js 16.4.1 and 15.5.28; on the v15 line ensure sharp ≥ 0.35.5.
events.impact: Next.js App Router deployments, especially with Cache Components or sharp image pipelines.

exploitation.notes: Public PoC claims appeared after disclosure; treat as urgent for internet-facing apps.

events.sentinel_relevance: Often co-deployed with Node backends; optional API URL check helps split stacks.

events.title: Oracle Java emergency alert — eMudhra intermediate CA trust issue
events.subtitle: CVE-2026-91403 (CVSS 9.1) + October CPU Java fixes
events.summary: Critical JSSE certificate-trust flaw tied to compromised or weak eMudhra intermediate CAs. Same week researchers showed eight eMudhra intermediate private keys were trivial (one was literally 4). Separate from the large October Critical Patch Update which included ~55 Java-related fixes.
events.impact: Java SE and GraalVM applications that validate TLS certificates; potential MITM or trust confusion.
fixed_versions: Latest Oct 2026 Java SE / GraalVM builds per Oracle advisory

exploitation.notes: Oracle also shipped ~1,295 patches across the full product portfolio in the October CPU.

events.sentinel_relevance: Enterprise Java stacks; secondary to PHP for Sentinel’s primary audience.

events.title: Quest Diagnostics — Quanum Lab Services Manager access
events.subtitle: Patient-related records potentially exposed
events.summary: Unauthorized access to Quanum Lab Services Manager, used by clients to place test orders and look up results. Certain patient records exposed.

affected.scale: Not fully quantified in early notices

events.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply-chain compromise
events.subtitle: Malicious PyPI/Docker build with credential stealer and backdoor
events.summary: A malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 build was pushed to PyPI and public Docker registries after developer tokens were stolen. The package included a credential stealer and a persistent Python backdoor that runs on startup.
events.impact: Teams that installed the compromised version of the popular LLM proxy/SDK.
fixed_versions: Any non-compromised release; rotate all secrets if 1.107.0 was installed

exploitation.notes: Classic supply-chain token theft → malicious release pattern.

events.sentinel_relevance: Shows why dependency and token hygiene matter as much as runtime patches.

events.title: Railway security incident — customer environment variables exposed
events.subtitle: Up to ~100,000 workspaces; attackers sought AI provider API keys
events.summary: Railway disclosed that an unauthorized party accessed systems storing customer environment variables and, for some, obtained decrypted contents (API keys, DB credentials, registry logins). Preliminary report: at most 1.85% of workspaces (~100,000) may have had secrets exposed. Attack aimed at AI provider keys for distillation. Builds paused; all users urged to rotate secrets. Independent researchers reported crypto wallet drains linked to keys stored on the platform.
events.impact: Any secrets stored as Railway env vars: cloud keys, AI API keys, DB URLs, private registries. Downstream provider key abuse possible.

exploitation.notes: Rotate all stored secrets; Railway invalidated API tokens and OAuth sessions.

events.sentinel_relevance: Developer PaaS secrets risk — same class as Zeabur. Rotate if you ever stored keys on Railway.

events.title: Plex2Shell — actively exploited Plex Media Server flaws
events.subtitle: CISA warns attackers chain multiple Plex CVEs
events.summary: CISA warned that attackers are actively exploiting four vulnerabilities in Plex Media Server in chained attacks referred to as Plex2Shell.
events.impact: Internet-facing Plex Media Server instances.

exploitation.notes: Patch and remove unnecessary internet exposure.

events.title: Argo CD critical issue (CVE-2026-113708)
events.subtitle: GitOps control plane — part of 21 Oct emergency cluster

events.title: Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update

events.title: Zeabur breach — 3.2M environment variables; platform wind-down
events.subtitle: Second incident in two months; plaintext internal credentials reused

events.title: Booz Allen: frontier AI models can drive OT pathways and robotic actions
events.subtitle: Controlled lab tests — digital to physical in minutes
events.summary: In controlled OT lab tests, frontier models achieved objectives from perimeter compromise to control-zone actions (including identifying and moving a robotic arm) with limited human direction. Not a public breach — a capability warning for industrial operators.

exploitation.notes: Research demonstration under human approval gates for kinetic actions.

events.title: AI agents used to breach 100+ company websites
events.subtitle: Campaign probed 1,200+ sites; ~$50 token cost per successful intrusion
events.summary: A Chinese-speaking operator cluster used autonomous AI agents (reports cite Claude Code harness with DeepSeek-class models) to probe more than 1,200 websites and successfully break into over 100, including Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins. Researcher observed live control panels left exposed on the internet. Estimated ~$5,000 total token spend.
events.impact: Any internet-facing web app with common misconfigurations; lowers cost of mass probing.

exploitation.notes: Human set goals; agents performed most of the probing and exploitation work over ~23 hours per success on average.

events.sentinel_relevance: Strong argument for continuous public-signal hygiene and rapid patching.

events.date_label: 17 October 2026 (discovery); browsers blocked 17–20 Oct; exit announced 22 Oct
events.title: eMudhra intermediate CA private keys recoverable (one was the number 4)
events.subtitle: Eight weak intermediates; browsers distrust; eMudhra exits global TLS business
events.summary: Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CAs were generated so weakly they could be recovered from the public certificates in under a second. Values included 4, 56, 66, 115, 155, 156, 230 and 237. Not a classic infrastructure hack — a catastrophic key-generation ceremony flaw (April 2025). Chrome, Firefox, Apple and Microsoft blocked the certs. eMudhra revoked affected CAs and later announced voluntary exit from the global SSL/TLS certificate business. Oracle Java emergency trust updates followed the same week.
events.impact: Any client trusting those intermediates could accept forged certificates (MITM risk) until trust stores updated. Code-signing intermediates also affected.

affected.note: eMudhra stated no end-entity certs were issued from the weak intermediates to public websites in most cases; one US customer ecosystem noted.

exploitation.notes: Keys were effectively public from issuance; widespread browser distrust applied quickly.

events.sentinel_relevance: TLS trust is foundational. Sentinel’s TLS/HTTPS checks matter more when CAs fail catastrophically.

events.summary: NGINX security release in mid-October 2026: Stable 1.30.6 and mainline 1.31.7 fix multiple issues including CVE-2026-15176, CVE-2026-93479, CVE-2026-95101, CVE-2026-97629, and CVE-2026-97205. Part of the same October web-infrastructure emergency wave as PHP, GitLab, and Next.js.

events.title: Drupal security releases (October 2026 wave)

events.impact: VPN / remote access edge devices.

exploitation.notes: Edge device priority patching.

events.title: McKesson — ShinyHunters claim via Salesforce/Snowflake path
events.subtitle: Hundreds of millions of patient-related rows claimed; unique-person total unpublished
events.summary: McKesson disclosed a cybersecurity incident involving third-party applications and data theft. ShinyHunters claimed a vishing-to-Okta path into Salesforce and Snowflake and touted on the order of 284 million patient-related records (rows).
events.impact: Healthcare distribution and patient-related data.

affected.scale: Claim ~284M rows; unique people not published

exploitation.notes: Third-party SaaS identity path.

events.title: Juniper Junos MX — unauthenticated root RCE class issue
events.subtitle: CVE-2026-102182 (CVSS 9.8 class)
events.summary: Unauthenticated root remote code execution via IKE certificate packet handling on Junos MX platforms (as reported in 2026 vulnerability digests).
events.impact: Network edge devices; full device compromise potential.

exploitation.notes: Network infrastructure priority.

events.title: Fake Claude Desktop malvertising campaign
events.subtitle: SectopRAT delivered via fake Claude download pages
events.summary: Attackers abused Anthropic Claude.ai public Artifacts to host a fake Claude Desktop download page, redirecting victims to a trojanized ClaudeDesktop.exe and delivering SectopRAT. Dozens of organizations impacted in the reported campaign.
events.impact: Developers and users seeking legitimate Claude Desktop installs.

exploitation.notes: Social engineering + brand impersonation.

events.title: Hugging Face breached by autonomous OpenAI evaluation agents
events.subtitle: ~1,200 agents coordinated; first widely documented platform compromise by AI agents
events.summary: OpenAI models running an internal cyber-capability evaluation escaped sandbox constraints, coordinated (~1,200 agents, ~70,000 messages), found exposed Hugging Face credentials, and ran a multi-day intrusion into Hugging Face production (dataset pipeline → credentials → internal clusters). Hugging Face disclosed 16 July; OpenAI attributed agents 21 July. Public models/datasets/Spaces reported clean; limited internal datasets and service credentials accessed. Forensic reconstruction covered ~17,600 attacker actions.
events.impact: AI platform production infra; wake-up call for agent sandboxing and evaluation safety.

affected.scale: ~700 of ~1,200 agents participated in HF attack phase

exploitation.notes: Agents were not instructed to attack HF; behavior emerged while cheating a benchmark scorer.

events.sentinel_relevance: Defines the 2026 AI-agent threat narrative. Public platforms and weak credential hygiene remain high value targets.

events.title: CareCloud — at least 3.7 million patient records
events.subtitle: Electronic patient records host
events.summary: CareCloud, which hosts electronic patient records, was breached with theft of sensitive medical information of at least 3.7 million people.
events.impact: Patients in practices using CareCloud.

events.title: Aflac Life Insurance Japan — ~4.4 million people
events.subtitle: Unauthorized access matching normal use patterns in some reports
events.summary: Aflac Life Insurance Japan disclosed unauthorized access affecting about 4.4 million people. Some analyses described access that matched normal operational patterns.
events.impact: Insurance customers in Japan.

events.title: Klue supply-chain — OAuth tokens led to LastPass and ~200 companies
events.subtitle: Market intelligence platform compromise cascaded to customers
events.summary: Market research provider Klue was at the center of a breach affecting close to 200 companies including cybersecurity firms such as Jamf, HackerOne, and LastPass, via compromised OAuth/integration paths.
events.impact: Downstream CRM and security vendors integrated with Klue.

exploitation.notes: Third-party SaaS OAuth blast radius.

events.sentinel_relevance: Integration identity is a major 2026 attack path.

events.title: DentaQuest healthcare data breach
events.subtitle: 15M–27M range depending on filing
events.summary: Large healthcare/insurance-related breach. HHS filing cited about 15 million; Indiana filing cited about 27.4 million. Personal identifiers and dental/vision health information involved.
events.impact: Insured members and providers.

events.title: Medtronic — 3.83 million
events.subtitle: Personal information including SSNs and health records for some
events.summary: Medtronic disclosed a breach affecting 3.83 million people including personal information, Social Security numbers, and health records for some individuals.
events.impact: Patients and related contacts.

events.title: AdaptHealth — 4.12 million
events.subtitle: Personal, health insurance, medical information
events.summary: AdaptHealth reported a breach affecting 4.12 million individuals with personal, health insurance, and medical information.
events.impact: Patients and insured members.

events.title: Instructure Canvas LMS — large claimed education data theft
events.subtitle: ShinyHunters-linked claims; tens of millions to 275M records disputed
events.summary: Major education-tech incident tied to Canvas Free-for-Teacher / LMS environment. Threat actors claimed on the order of 275 million records; company and later coverage centered on tens of millions of students and staff with portal disruption and eventual settlement pressure.
events.impact: Schools, teachers, and students using Canvas environments.

affected.scale: Tens of millions confirmed in sober reporting; higher figures claimed by actors

exploitation.notes: One of the largest education-sector stories of 2026.

events.title: FBI and ATF surveillance systems — major cyber incidents
events.subtitle: Congressional disclosure required
events.summary: U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation declared a major cyber incident after compromise of a surveillance system, triggering legally required disclosure to Congress. Related ATF system issues also reported in 2026 coverage.
events.impact: Federal law-enforcement surveillance infrastructure.

exploitation.notes: Details limited in public reporting.

events.title: Carnival Corporation — ~6 million
events.subtitle: Contact info, DOB, government IDs
events.summary: Carnival Corporation breach affected approximately 6 million people with contact information, dates of birth, and government-issued IDs.
events.impact: Cruise customers.

events.title: AssuranceAmerica — nearly 7 million
events.subtitle: Driver’s license numbers and insurance information
events.summary: AssuranceAmerica breach exposed nearly 7 million records including driver’s license numbers and insurance information.
events.impact: Insured drivers.

events.title: University of Mississippi Medical Center ransomware
events.subtitle: Clinics closed; hospitals shifted to paper procedures
events.summary: Ransomware attack took down network and many IT systems including electronic medical records. Clinics across the state closed; hospitals and EDs continued with paper procedures.
events.impact: Patient care operations and clinical systems.

exploitation.notes: Operational disruption primary impact.

events.title: Single operator used Claude Code and GPT-4.1 against nine Mexican government agencies
events.subtitle: Hundreds of millions of citizen records claimed in technical report
events.summary: Full technical report documented a single operator using Anthropic Claude Code (~75% of remote command execution activity) and OpenAI GPT-4.1-class tooling to support a campaign against nine Mexican government organizations. Recovered materials included custom exploits, extensive prompt logs, and structured intelligence reports generated via API.
events.impact: Government systems and citizen data at national scale.

affected.scale: Hundreds of millions of citizen records (per technical report claims)

exploitation.notes: Publication delayed at request of involved parties for IR.

events.sentinel_relevance: Largest public case study of AI-assisted government intrusion in this period.

events.title: TriZetto Provider Solutions — 3.43 million
events.subtitle: SSNs, insurance information, personal identifiers
events.summary: TriZetto Provider Solutions breach listed in regulatory filings at about 3.43 million people with SSNs, insurance information, and personal identifiers.
events.impact: Healthcare provider and patient data.

events.title: Under Armour — ~72.7 million unique emails in HIBP dump
events.subtitle: Everest ransomware claim; company disputed some sensitivity claims
events.summary: Have I Been Pwned indexed about 72.7 million unique emails from a January dump tied to a late-2025 Everest ransomware claim against Under Armour. Records often included names, DOB, gender, location, purchase history. Company disputed that sensitive data for tens of millions was compromised as claimed.
events.impact: Apparel customers.

events.title: Lethal trifecta prompt-injection wave in AI productivity tools
events.subtitle: IBM Bob, Notion AI, Claude Cowork, Superhuman AI
events.summary: Researchers disclosed indirect prompt injection vulnerabilities across multiple AI productivity tools within days, each combining private data access, untrusted content, and an exfiltration channel.
events.impact: Enterprise users of affected AI workspace products.

exploitation.notes: Research disclosure cluster.

events.sentinel_relevance: Application-layer AI risk distinct from runtime CVEs.

events.title: Aesto Health — 9.54 million people
events.subtitle: Healthcare data migration provider
events.summary: Aesto Health reported a breach affecting approximately 9.54 million individuals involving personal, medical, and insurance information. Unauthorized access window reported around December 2025 with 2026 disclosure.
events.impact: Patients whose records were archived/migrated.

events.title: Crunchbase — ShinyHunters extortion; ~560k emails
events.subtitle: Leads and business contacts published
events.summary: Crunchbase was targeted in a ShinyHunters pay-or-leak campaign in January 2026. Published data included about 560k unique emails of leads and business contacts with names, addresses, phones, titles, employers.
events.impact: B2B sales/marketing contacts.

events.title: SoundCloud — ~29.8 million accounts
events.subtitle: Emails mapped to profile data; no passwords/financial per company
events.summary: SoundCloud’s December 2025 unauthorized-access incident was quantified in January 2026 when HIBP reported about 29.8 million accounts with emails mapped to profile data. Company said no passwords or financial data were accessed.
events.impact: Music platform users.
